Impact: No IPA user or group resolves here (apart from nscd/memory caches), and no IPA login works.

RULED OUT
enrollment configuration is present; SSSD is configured for the IPA domain; the IPA server name resolves; LDAP SRV rec
ords exist; Kerberos SRV records exist; the server answers on HTTPS; the server answers on LDAP; the server answers on K
erberos (TCP); the server's certificate is trusted; the clocks agree; the host keytab holds this host's key; the KDC acc
epts this host's key; the SSSD configuration is valid; the PAM service uses SSSD
RESOLUTION
For 'SSSD is not running': Start SSSD (risk MEDIUM; ipa-diagnose never runs it)
Verified in a live lab on FreeIPA 4.13.4 / fedora-43 (the maintainer has not promoted it to built-in verified). Chec
k each step before running it.
✓ ipa-diagnose is running as root (starting a system service needs root)
1. Start only sssd.service; no other service is started or stopped
systemctl start sssd.service
Expected: the command returns without an error and sssd.service is active. If it fails, it stays stopped and 'sys
temctl status sssd' shows why.
What changes: sssd.service goes from inactive to running. SSSD reads its existing configuration and cache; nothing i
s edited or deleted.
Rollback: Stop it again (back to the state it was in) -> systemctl stop sssd.service
Note: This starts SSSD; it does not establish why it stopped. If it stopped because of a failure (see the last resul
t and log line above), the same cause can stop it again.
NEXT READ-ONLY STEPS
systemctl status sssd (read-only)
journalctl -u sssd -n 30 (read-only)
VERIFY
After a fix, run: ipa-diagnose client --verify --user alice --service sshd (fresh checks; compares with this run)
- sssd.service is active
- SSSD resolves the group admins (present in every IPA domain)
LIMITATIONS
No login is attempted and no credential is tested: RUNTIME ACCESS and AUTHENTICATION are never reported as PASS.
